Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield Technologies' results for the third quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Taylor Voss, Chief Financial Officer; Riley Kim, Chief Technology Officer, and Morgan Lee, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. CyberShield Technologies had an exceptional third quarter, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. We are seeing significant traction with our cloud-native security platform and are benefiting from the increased focus on cybersecurity across all industries. The impact of our new AI-powered threat detection is evident in the reduced incident response times reported by our customers, with many achieving over 35% faster mean time to respond compared to legacy systems.

Our strategy is centered around five core pillars: relentless R&D investment to outpace evolving threats, superior competitive win rates that demonstrate our product leadership, high net dollar retention reflecting customer stickiness, a thriving channel partner ecosystem driving scalable growth, and an optimistic full-year revenue and profitability outlook fueled by market tailwinds.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Voss to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Voss: Thank you, Jordan. As Jordan highlighted, we had a remarkable third quarter. Revenue reached $285 million, reflecting a 35% year-over-year increase. This growth was fueled by both new customer acquisition and expansion within our existing customer base. Our gross margin remained strong at 80%, demonstrating our ability to scale efficiently. Operating expenses were $200 million, and net income was $75 million, translating to $0.55 per share. We are increasing our guidance for the full year based on these outstanding results.

Let me dive deeper into some of our key strategic levers, starting with our R&D investment as a percentage of revenue, which underscores our unwavering commitment to innovation in an industry where cyber threats evolve faster than ever—from AI-powered phishing campaigns and polymorphic ransomware to supply chain exploits reminiscent of SolarWinds. Staying ahead requires relentless investment, and I'm proud to report that we've maintained a robust R&D intensity that positions us as a leader among hyperscalers and pure-play cybersecurity firms.

For the third quarter, our R&D spend totaled $148 million, representing 19.2% of total revenue—up from 17.8% in Q3 2023 and a sequential increase from 18.7% in Q2 2024. On a trailing 12-month basis, this clocks in at 18.5% of our $2.1 billion ARR, which is in line with top-tier peers like CrowdStrike at around 18-20% and Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Cloud group hovering near 22%. This uptick reflects both organic growth in our innovation pipeline and targeted acquisitions, including our recent bolt-on of QuantumSafe Labs to accelerate post-quantum cryptography development.

Year-over-year, R&D as a percentage has trended upward by 140 basis points, fueled by a 28% increase in absolute R&D dollars. This isn't dilution—it's deliberate scaling. We've shifted about 15% of our R&D budget toward AI/ML-driven initiatives, including our next-gen Autonomous Threat Response engine, which leverages generative AI for real-time behavioral analytics and zero-day prediction. Early pilots with Fortune 500 clients in financial services have shown a 35% reduction in mean time to respond compared to legacy SIEM tools like Splunk or Elastic.

Regionally, we're tailoring our intensity. In North America, which accounts for 52% of our revenue, R&D allocation remains steady at around 18%, focused on enhancing our Cortex XDR platform extensions for hybrid cloud environments—think integrations with AWS Nitro Enclaves and Azure Confidential Computing to counter insider threats. EMEA, at 28% of revenue, has pushed our blended rate higher, with 22% R&D intensity there due to stringent regulations like the NIS2 Directive and DORA. We're pouring resources into sovereign data residency solutions, including our EU-specific Zero-Trust Fabric, which complies with Schrems II while supporting multi-cloud federation.

APAC is the growth hotspot—and the R&D hotspot too—at 20% regional intensity on 15% of revenue. State-sponsored actors from nation-state APT groups like APT41 and Lazarus are ramping up, with ransomware incidents up 45% year-over-year per our Threat Intelligence Report. We've doubled down on SASE-plus offerings, embedding ML-based Deception-as-a-Service to mimic assets and lure attackers, directly competing with Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange. This has driven 40% ARR growth in Japan and India, where we're partnering with NTT and Reliance Jio for telco-edge security.

Strategically, this R&D posture is about future-proofing. We're not just reacting; we're anticipating. Key initiatives include a $25 million allocation to NIST PQC standards like Kyber and Dilithium, with beta rollout in Q1 2025 to protect against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks; our ShieldAI lab developing red-team simulations using reinforcement learning to harden models against prompt injection and data poisoning—critical as competitors like SentinelOne integrate similar into their Singularity platform; and $18 million into OT/IoT Security Mesh for securing industrial control systems with protocols for Modbus and OPC-UA, targeting the 30% surge in manufacturing breaches per Mandiant's M-Trends.

We've optimized efficiency too—non-GAAP R&D headcount grew only 12% year-over-year to 1,850 engineers, thanks to our Bangalore and Tel Aviv R&D hubs, where burn rates are 25-30% below Silicon Valley norms. This keeps us agile amid macroeconomic headwinds like elevated interest rates squeezing VC funding for startups.

Looking forward, we guide R&D at 18-20% of revenue for FY2025, with potential for 19.5% if we close our proposed acquisition of EdgeDefend for $450 million in network detection tech. This sustains our 25%+ gross margins while delivering 2-3x ROI on innovations through upsell—evidenced by our 125% net retention rate.

Next, let's turn to our competitive win rates, a leading indicator of our product-market fit in this hyper-competitive landscape, where customers demand platform consolidation amid escalating threats like ransomware-as-a-service and AI-powered phishing. In Q3, we delivered a headline competitive win rate of 68%, up 400 basis points quarter-over-quarter from 64% in Q2 and a 6 percentage point improvement year-over-year from 62% in Q3 2023. This marks our strongest quarterly performance in two years and reflects the impact of our Unified Threat Fabric platform strategy. For context, the broader industry benchmark per IDC's latest Competitive Displacement Tracker hovers around 55-60% for Tier 1 vendors, so we're significantly outpacing the field.

By solution area: In Endpoint Detection and Response, we hit 72%, displacing CrowdStrike's Falcon in 68% of head-to-head deals, thanks to our NeuralShield AI engine's 99.7% true positive rate in MITRE ATT&CK Evaluations Round 3—outscoring Falcon by 1.2 points—and MTTD under 2 minutes. Cloud-Native Security (CNAPP/SSE) was a standout at 75%, winning 82% against Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange with agentless scanning for multi-cloud. Network Security (NGFW/SASE) at 58%, gaining at 62% versus Palo Alto's Prisma Access, with legacy displacements from Check Point and Fortinet.

Head-to-head: Across 1,247 deals, 70% vs. CrowdStrike (superior cost-per-endpoint at $18/user/year and 40% faster MTTR), 65% vs. Palo Alto (25% lower TCO), 72% vs. SentinelOne/Microsoft Defender, and 85% against legacy like Symantec.

Regionally: North America 70% (CMMC 2.0 and DoD), EMEA 66% (GDPR and zero-trust), APAC 58% improving (Japan/India wins).

Driving this: $150 million R&D in AI/ML for autonomous playbook generation (35% less analyst fatigue), shortened PoC cycles to 42 days via CyberRange, and platformization with 72% of wins expanding to 3+ modules. We expect Q4 at 70-72% with QuantumShield.

Shifting to net dollar retention—or NDR—which captures the strength of our business model. In Q3 FY24, NDR was 119%, the fifth straight quarter above 115%, up 200 basis points sequentially and 700 basis points year-over-year. This highlights the sticky nature of our platform amid 30% ransomware surge and Log4Shell exploits.

Components: Gross retention at 98%, with 99% renewals for long-tenure customers via Nebula orchestration. Expansion added 21 points, $28 million net ARR (35% YoY), from SASE bundles (42% of top customers), threat intelligence upsells (28%), and 5-7% pricing on SLAs.

Enterprises hit 128%, North America 122% (CISA mandates), EMEA 115% (NIS2/GDPR), APAC 112% (Cybersecurity Act). $150 million R&D in Sentinel AI predicts 85% zero-days. Q4 outlook 120-122%, targeting 70% multi-module adoption.

Our channel partners drove 65% of Q3 revenue—$185.4 million, 28% YoY growth, 12% QoQ, with $1.12 billion of $1.65 billion ARR (32% YoY, 128% NRR). Top strategic partners (Accenture, Deloitte) 42% ($77.8 million, 35% YoY, $450K ACV avg), distributors (Ingram) 28% ($51.9 million, 22% YoY), MSPs/VARs 22% ($40.8 million, 25% YoY).

Americas 52% ($96.4 million, 30% YoY, CISA/SolarWinds), EMEA 28% ($51.9 million, 26% YoY, NIS2), APAC 15% ($27.8 million, 18% YoY). $45 million in enablement, Partner Program 2.0, API integrations. FY25 channel 68-70%.

Finally, our full-year 2024 outlook: Raising revenue to $1.22 billion to $1.28 billion, 32-38% growth. ARR ended Q2 at $1.05 billion (42% YoY, 118% NDR), expect $1.30 billion+. Cloud Security 45% ($560 million), Endpoint/XDR 30% ($380 million), IAM 15% ($190 million), OT/IoT 10% ($120 million). NA 65% ($800 million), EMEA 20% ($260 million), APAC 15% ($190 million).

Profitability: Non-GAAP gross 79-81%, op income $320-350 million (26-27% margins), GAAP $220-250 million, EBITDA $380-410 million, EPS $2.45-2.65. Rule-of-40+ at 70+.

Next, Riley Kim will provide more technical details.

Riley Kim: Thank you, Taylor. We continue to innovate and push the boundaries of what's possible in cybersecurity. Our team is focused on developing cutting-edge solutions that address the evolving threat landscape. We are investing heavily in research and development to stay ahead of the curve and deliver unparalleled value to our customers. Key areas of focus include advancing our NeuralShield AI for generative threat hunting, quantum-resistant crypto stacks compliant with NIST standards, and OT/IoT meshes for ICS protocols amid surging manufacturing breaches. These efforts directly support our competitive edges and customer expansions.

Morgan Lee: Thank you. Cybersecurity is paramount, and we are taking proactive measures to protect our customers and ourselves. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance, from FedRAMP High to NIS2 and GDPR, ensuring our platform fortifies against nation-state APTs and ransomware.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the question and answer session. First question comes from Sarah Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Chen: Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Taylor, could you expand on the R&D intensity trends and how they tie into your competitive win rates?

Taylor Voss: Thanks, Sarah. As I detailed, our 19.2% R&D in Q3, trending to 18-20% FY25, directly fuels wins like 72% in EDR via NeuralShield's MITRE superiority and 75% in CNAPP. The $150 million AI investments shortened PoCs and boosted platform adoption, driving that 68% headline rate.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Patel: Great results. Jordan or Taylor, thoughts on net dollar retention sustainability given macro pressures, and channel partner contributions?

Jordan Hale: Mike, our 119% NDR is mission-critical stickiness, with 98% gross retention and 21-point expansions from SASE and AI upsells. Channels at 65% of revenue, growing 28% YoY, amplify this—top partners like Accenture delivering $450K ACVs in bundled deals.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Torres with JPMorgan.

Lisa Torres: Impressive guidance raise. Riley, how are technical innovations like post-quantum and GenAI defenses positioning you against peers in APAC and OT?

Riley Kim: Lisa, our $25 million PQC push with Kyber/Dilithium betas and ShieldAI red-teaming harden against quantum threats, while OT meshes target 30% breach surges. In APAC, SASE-plus Deception-as-a-Service counters APT41/Lazarus, driving 40% ARR growth via NTT partnerships.

Operator: Next question comes from David Kwon with Barclays.

David Kwon: Thanks. Taylor, walk us through the full-year profitability drivers and any risks to margins from acquisitions?

Taylor Voss: David, 79-81% gross margins from SaaS efficiencies and cloud shifts, with op margins expanding to 26-27% via 15% OpEx growth vs. 35% revenue. Acquisitions like QuantumSafe and EdgeDefend add amortization but deliver ROI through upsells; FCF over 120% of EBITDA mitigates risks.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Jordan Hale: Thank you all for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. Thank you to our dedicated employees, loyal customers, and valued partners.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
